title: Top 10 Strongest Aniimo Right Now | The Picks Tier Lists Agree On | Aniimo Guide
description: Ten Aniimo that many tier lists rate highly right now, grouped by role: damage, breakers, healers, regen and support, with notes on why guides keep naming them.

sections.heading: Who is strongest in Idyll
sections.script: Which Aniimo are really the strongest right now? Every guide seems to have a different answer, so in this video we do something more useful. We look at the tier lists that many guides publish, and we pick ten creatures that keep showing up near the top. One honest warning first. Strongest is partly opinion. Tier lists are early, they were written in the first weeks after launch, and they disagree about who deserves the top slot. So when we say many guides rate an Aniimo highly, that is exactly what we mean. We will skip the shaky numbers and stick to what the lists agree on. We will go role by role, because Aniimo is a team game, and a great team beats one great creature. Think of this as a shortlist you can trust, not a final verdict. If your favorite creature is missing, that does not make it bad. It only means the lists we checked did not agree on it strongly enough.

sections.heading: How to read a tier list
sections.script: Before the list, a quick word on how to read it. Every Aniimo has one of five roles. DPS deals the main damage. A Breaker drains the enemy's break meter to open a damage window. A Support adds buffs and debuffs. A Healer keeps the team alive, and a Regen restores energy for longer fights. You bring a party of four. That means a top damage dealer is not automatically better than a top healer, because they do different jobs. Most guides also say the lists rank final forms, so a creature you just caught may still need to evolve. And the lists change with updates, so treat everything here as a strong starting point, not a law. One more tip is to read the reasons, not only the letters. A creature in a lower tier can still be perfect for your team, if it fills a role you are missing and you enjoy using it.

sections.heading: Damage dealers: Irisalis
sections.script: Let us start with damage, and with the name that shows up on almost every list, Irisalis. This Grass type legendary is ranked as one of the top damage dealers by many guides, and tools that rank Aniimo by stats also place it near the very top. It arrived with the version one point one update, and you earn it through the Legendary Journey event rather than catching it in the open world. That event window runs until December tenth, twenty twenty six, so if you want it, do not wait until the last week. If you can only chase one prestige pick right now, many guides would tell you this is the one. A legendary is not a magic win button, of course. Even the best damage dealer needs a Breaker to open the fight and a way to recover energy, so we will cover those roles next.

sections.heading: Damage dealers: Fulmintis and Malevsera
sections.script: Next, two more damage picks that guides like. Fulmintis is a damage dealer that appears high in several tier lists, and one guide even calls it the best damage dealer in the game. It is also used as the main attacker in community boss strategies. Then there is Malevsera. Many guides describe it as a self sustaining carry, which means it can hit hard and still look after itself during a long fight. That makes it a friendly choice for players who do not want to babysit their health bar. Both are placed in the upper tiers, even if the lists disagree on exactly how high. If you can only afford the time to raise one attacker, check its evolution requirements first, because some need a boss defeated or a special item.

sections.heading: Breakers: Wavwal and Geoclaw
sections.script: Now the Breakers, the creatures that make bosses stagger. Wavwal is a favorite of several guides. It is known for solid bulk and for protecting the team with a shield, which makes it useful in long battles. Geoclaw is the other name that comes up again and again. Guides describe it as a Breaker that stacks ice effects on the target to crack the stance bar open. Both are in the top half of the lists we checked. If your damage dealer feels weak against a boss, the real problem is often that nobody is breaking it, so a good Breaker can feel like a big power upgrade. Breakers also matter because a staggered enemy is a lot easier to hit and takes bonus damage. Many players underestimate how much faster a fight becomes when the stance bar is broken on time.

sections.heading: Healers: Gracewing and Glacy
sections.script: Healers next. Gracewing is probably the most consistent name across the lists, and one source calls it the number one healer. It is a support creature that mostly keeps allies alive, so it needs a real attacker beside it. Glacy is the other healer that guides like. It is described as an all rounder that heals the whole team over time, and it is another popular pick. Because a party only has four slots, most players run just one healer. Picking between these two is mostly about taste and about what else is in your team. Either one makes tough fights much calmer. If you ever play in a group, the healer role matters even more, because bosses hit hard and a single mistake can take a teammate out of the fight.

sections.heading: Regen: Somniwing and Besauce
sections.script: Energy matters in Aniimo, because your best skills cost it. That is why Regen creatures are so popular. Somniwing is rated highly by many guides for restoring energy and helping the team recover it faster. Besauce is the other Regen pick that appears often. Guides describe it as flexible, because it returns energy when you use low cost skills and fits into almost any team. Community boss strategies even list Somniwing and Besauce as the regen slot. If you run out of energy mid fight, one of these two is probably missing from your party. Regen is the least glamorous role, but it keeps your whole rotation running smoothly, and that is why it appears so often in strong team examples.

sections.heading: Support: Tromber
sections.script: Our tenth pick is a support. Tromber is a Wind type that guides describe as a crowd control support, and it also boosts Wind damage for the team. It is listed in the upper tiers by more than one guide, and one ranking even places it among its very top creatures. Support slots are the ones players forget, but a support can stack buffs and debuffs so your damage dealer hits harder and your Breaker breaks faster. If you already have a damage dealer, a Breaker and a healer, Tromber is a smart way to fill the last slot, especially if your team leans on Wind. A quick reminder that one support is usually enough. The fourth slot is precious, so choose the creature that fixes the biggest hole in your party.

sections.heading: Why these ten
sections.script: Let us zoom out. These ten are Irisalis, Fulmintis, Malevsera, Wavwal, Geoclaw, Gracewing, Glacy, Somniwing, Besauce and Tromber. They are not a perfect ranking, and they are not in strict order. They are the creatures that many guides rate highly, grouped by what they do. Notice something important. Only a few of them are damage dealers, and the rest keep the team stable. That is a pattern across the lists. Players who win consistently build a balanced party with a damage dealer, a Breaker, healing or energy, and support, instead of stacking the biggest attackers they can find.

sections.heading: Build around your own pick
sections.script: So how do you use this? Start with one pick you actually like, then build around it. Add a Breaker if your attacker lacks one. Add healing or Regen if you keep running low. Remember elements too. A mixed team covers more weaknesses than a team of one type. And always check the evolution panel for any creature you want, because the requirements differ, and some need a boss defeated or a special item. A tier list tells you who is good in general. Your team, your playstyle and the boss in front of you decide who is best for you.

sections.heading: Who is on your team
sections.script: That is our list of ten Aniimo that many guides rate as the strongest right now. Which one would you put at the very top, and is there a favorite you think guides are underrating? Tell us in the comments, because we read them all. If this helped you, like the video and subscribe to HarryBeast Gaming for more Aniimo guides, tier lists and tips. Tier lists change with every update, so we will keep checking back. Thanks for watching, and see you in Idyll.
